items.title: Boulkiemdé : le Premier ministre met en eau les barrages de Kokologho et de Gouloré pour renforcer la production agricole
items.description: BURKINA-NANDO-INFRASTRUCTURES-HYDRO-AGRICOLES-MISE-EN-EAU Boulkiemdé : le Premier ministre met en eau les barrages de Kokologho et de Gouloré pour renforcer la production agricole Kokologho, 1er août 2026 (AIB) – Le Premier ministre, le camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a procédé samedi à la mise en eau officielle des barrages de Kokologho et de Gouloré, dans la province du Boulkiemdé, des infrastructures hydro-agricoles réalisées par l'Office national des barrages et des aménagements hydro-agricoles (ONBAH) afin de renforcer la production agricole et d'améliorer durablement les conditions de vie des populations. À Kokologho, le chef du Gouvernement a salué la réhabilitation complète d'un ouvrage dont la digue avait cédé depuis près de dix-huit ans, privant les producteurs d'un important potentiel de stockage d'eau. Réalisés en trois mois par l'ONBAH sur financement du budget de l'État, les travaux ont permis de restaurer entièrement le barrage et de porter sa capacité de retenue à plus de 800 000 m³. « Cela ouvre de bonnes perspectives, notamment l'aménagement d'un périmètre exploitable de près de 25 hectares », a déclaré le Premier ministre, annonçant le démarrage prochain des travaux d'aménagement hydro-agricole autour de l'ouvrage. Le directeur général de l'ONBAH, le camarade commandant Yaya Traoré, a indiqué que le barrage, construit en 1945 par les populations puis réhabilité une première fois en 1987, a bénéficié cette fois d'une intervention complète. Les travaux ont consisté notamment à protéger la digue côté amont, à la rehausser de 20 centimètres, à réhabiliter la prise d'eau ainsi que le bassin de dissipation et à curer près de 75 000 m³ de sédiments. La délégation gouvernementale s'est ensuite rendue à Gouloré où le Premier ministre a procédé à la mise en eau d'un barrage entièrement reconstruit par l'ONBAH. D'une capacité de plus de 1 020 000 m³, contre 80 000 m³ pour l'ancien ouvrage, ce barrage est doté d'une digue de 1 114 mètres, offrant de nouvelles perspectives en matière d'irrigation, de pisciculture et de développement d'activités génératrices de revenus. Pour le camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, ces réalisations traduisent la volonté du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, de conjuguer la reconquête du territoire avec l'amélioration durable des conditions de vie des populations. « Il faut donner aux populations les moyens de produire 365 jours sur 365 », a-t-il affirmé, précisant que ces infrastructures permettront de soutenir la production agricole tout au long de l'année et de créer des opportunités économiques au profit des femmes, des jeunes et de l'ensemble des producteurs. Le Premier ministre a également félicité l'ONBAH et le ministère en charge de l'Agriculture pour la qualité et la célérité des travaux, tout en annonçant que d'autres chantiers de barrages, de plus grande envergure, sont déjà en préparation. Il a enfin invité les populations riveraines à protéger ces ouvrages, réalisés grâce aux ressources propres de l'État, en respectant les zones de servitude et les règles de préservation des barrages afin d'en garantir la sécurité et la durabilité au bénéfice des générations futures. Agence d'information du Burkina FGB/PB

items.title: I’ll continue to guarantee freedom of religion – Tinubu
items.description: By Ishola Balogun President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his administration’s continued commitment to guaranteeing freedom of religion as entrenched in the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended). The President stated this at the commissioning of the Ansar-Ud-Deen Society of Nigeria (ADSN) National Headquarters (Hassanat Abebi Okunnu House), in Surulere, Lagos, on Saturday. The President, who was represented by the Attorney General of the Federation and the Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), said: “The government under my watch will continue to guarantee freedom of religion while encouraging religious organisations to promote tolerance, peaceful coexistence, and national unity.” Tinubu commended ADSN for its contributions to education, moral development, religious service, healthcare, humanitarian intervention, and community development over a century ago, describing the organisation as one of the foremost Islamic bodies in Nigeria. “Government alone cannot build the nation of our dreams. It requires strong partnerships with faith-based organisations that share the vision of building an enlightened, disciplined, and compassionate society. The Ansar-Ud-Deen Society has consistently demonstrated that religious organisations remain indispensable partners in national development,” he stated. President Tínubu lauded the donor of the Secretariat, Alhaji Femi Okunnu, for immortalising his late mother through the construction of the facility, describing the project as a lasting act of faith and generosity that will continue to serve humanity for generations. He also commended Okunnu’s integrity, humility, public service, adding that the Okunnu family is known with integrity, patriotism, and selfless service to Nigeria. Describing the late Alhaja Okunnu, President Tínubu said: “There can be no greater testimony to a person’s character than the quality of the children they leave behind. A tree is known by its fruits, and a mother’s legacy is most clearly reflected in the lives of those she nurtured. Looking at the accomplishments and impeccable reputation of her children, we need no further evidence that she was a woman of faith, noble character, discipline, and uncommon wisdom.” Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr Kadiri Hamzat, urged ADSN to preserve the organisation’s founding ideals by promoting education, moral values and righteous living, describing knowledge as the greatest asset for national development. Hamzat, who lauded the pioneer of ADSN, said they helped change the narrative at a time when many Muslim children were discouraged from pursuing Western education by establishing schools and encouraging learning, adding that present generations continue to benefit from those efforts. He said: Sadly, one of the greatest challenges confronting our society today is the erosion of our values. We hear young people saying, “Education is a scam.” Others glorify ignorance and reject the pursuit of knowledge. Our Islamic educational institutions must confront this dangerous trend because no nation can develop if its citizens are not properly educated.” The National President of ADSN, Alhaji Mosediq Kazeem, said the new National Headquarters was a fulfilment of a long-held vision and a renewed commitment to faith, education, and national development. He said that the Secretariat represents more than a physical structure, describing it as a symbol of vision, sacrifice, faith, and service, adding that after 103 years of existence, the Society is preparing for an even greater future by strengthening its institutions, embracing innovation, empowering young people, and sustaining its tradition of excellence. He said: “For over a century, we have worked alongside government in nurturing responsible citizens and building stronger communities. Our contribution is measured not simply by the schools we have built or the projects we have undertaken, but by the generations of Nigerians we have helped to shape, men and women whose lives reflect scholarship, integrity, patriotism and service.” The post I’ll continue to guarantee freedom of religion – Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kankan : une mineure condamnée à deux ans de prison pour le meurtre d’un homme présenté comme son mari
items.description: Le Tribunal de première instance de Kankan a rendu, ce 31 juillet 2026, son verdict dans l’affaire Boh Fanta Camara, poursuivie pour le meurtre d’Ousmane Diané. Âgée de 13 ans au moment des faits, survenus en 2024 dans le district de Bathè Soila, la jeune fille avait reconnu devant le tribunal avoir poignardé Ousmane Diané, alors qu’il dormait. À l’audience du 27 juillet, elle avait expliqué avoir été conduite chez cet homme dans le cadre d’un mariage auquel elle affirme s’être opposée. Elle avait également déclaré avoir subi des violences physiques et sexuelles durant les onze jours passés dans son foyer. Selon sa version, le coup de couteau n’avait pas pour objectif de tuer, mais de faire renoncer l’homme au mariage. Entendu lors du procès, un proche de la famille avait indiqué qu’une promesse de mariage aurait été faite dès la naissance de la jeune fille, après le décès de son frère jumeau. Devenue adolescente, elle se serait ensuite opposée à cette union. Au terme des débats, le tribunal a retenu l’excuse de minorité ainsi que des circonstances atténuantes et a condamné Boh Fanta Camara à deux ans d’emprisonnement. Le verdict met ainsi fin au procès engagé quelques jours plus tôt, devant le Tribunal de première instance de Kankan.

items.title: Une nuit 100 % cubaine le 4 août au Festival de Boukornine
items.description: Le Festival international de Boukornine met les rythmes latinos à l'honneur pour une soirée exceptionnelle ce mardi 4 août 2026 à 22h à l'occasion d'un double concert en plein air. L'affiche réunira Raúl Paz, figure incontournable et grande voix de la scène cubaine contemporaine, ainsi que le groupe Somos Nai. Amateurs de salsa, de bachata et de musiques du monde sont attendus sous les étoiles de Boukornine pour un événement qui s'annonce chaleureux et festif. Les billets sont d'ores et déjà disponibles aux tarifs de 20 DT et 30 DT, notamment via la billetterie en ligne du festival. « Salseros, bachateros, amoureux des rythmes latinos et de la vraie musique cubaine : cette soirée est faite pour vous » , commente les organisateurs. Y. N. L’article Une nuit 100 % cubaine le 4 août au Festival de Boukornine est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Fifa : Faut-il chercher toujours plus d’argent ou renforcer l’universalité du football au nom de l’équité ? (Par Dr Papa Abdoulaye Seck)
items.description: Au moment même où le monde du football s'interroge sur les enseignements de la Coupe du monde 2026, une autre question, plus fondamentale encore, s'impose : la FIFA doit-elle poursuivre une logique de financiarisation ou renforcer l'universalité du football au nom de l'équité ? Le projet d'ouverture du capital de la société chargée des activités commerciales de la FIFA à des investisseurs privés marque un tournant majeur. Il ne s'agit pas d'une simple opération financière. Il pose une question de principe : la Coupe du monde est-elle un patrimoine universel de l'humanité ou un actif financier destiné à accroître toujours davantage les revenus de ses détenteurs ? La Coupe du monde constitue le sommet de la pyramide du football mondial. Elle célèbre l'universalité de ce sport, la fraternité entre les peuples et l'égalité des chances sur le terrain. Depuis près d'un siècle, elle rassemble des milliards de femmes et d'hommes autour d'une passion commune. Cette universalité est son bien le plus précieux. Elle ne saurait être fragilisée par une logique où la finance finirait par dicter la gouvernance. Le très haut niveau exige non seulement l'excellence sportive, mais aussi une gouvernance exemplaire fondée sur l'équité, la transparence et le respect des peuples. Or, la Coupe du monde 2026 a révélé plusieurs défis majeurs : le coût parfois prohibitif des déplacements, des billets et des hébergements, les difficultés rencontrées par de nombreux supporters, notamment africains, pour obtenir des visas, les interrogations suscitées par certaines décisions arbitrales ainsi que le coût élevé des droits de retransmission, qui prive parfois des millions de passionnés d'un accès normal à la compétition. Voilà les véritables priorités. Avant de rechercher de nouveaux montages financiers, la FIFA devrait d'abord répondre à ces interrogations. Renforcer la crédibilité des compétitions, garantir leur accessibilité et préserver leur vocation universelle constituent des exigences bien plus urgentes que l'ouverture du capital à des investisseurs privés. À cet égard, la réaction de l'UEFA mérite d'être saluée. En exprimant ses réserves, elle rappelle qu'une réforme d'une telle portée ne peut être appréciée à la seule lumière des considérations financières. La Coupe du monde est un patrimoine sportif, culturel et humain qui appartient aux peuples. En revanche, la position de la CAF étonne et inquiète. Elle paraît s'inscrire dans cette orientation sans qu'un véritable débat public n'ait permis d'en démontrer la nécessité, les avantages ou les conséquences pour le football africain. Plus préoccupant encore, aucun argument suffisamment étayé ne semble avoir été présenté pour justifier un tel alignement. En matière de gouvernance, le consensus ne vaut que lorsqu'il est éclairé. À défaut, il risque davantage de traduire un réflexe d'alignement qu'une conviction librement construite. L'Afrique mérite mieux. Premier réservoir mondial de talents, continent de la jeunesse et de la passion footballistique, elle ne peut demeurer une simple caisse de résonance des décisions prises ailleurs. Elle doit être une force de réflexion, de proposition et d'influence. Son devoir est d'interroger, d'évaluer et, lorsque cela est nécessaire, de contester les réformes qui risquent d'altérer les principes fondateurs du football mondial. Au fond, la question dépasse largement le football. Elle renvoie à notre conception de la mondialisation. Devons-nous accepter que les grands patrimoines universels soient progressivement soumis aux seules logiques du marché, ou devons-nous préserver leur vocation première : servir les peuples ? Ma réponse est sans ambiguïté :le football appartient d'abord aux peuples. La Coupe du monde constitue un bien commun de l'humanité. Elle ne doit ni être confisquée par les intérêts économiques ni devenir un simple actif financier. L'Afrique ne doit pas accompagner cette réflexion ; sa voix doit raisonner : faire du football un langage universel au service des peuples avant celui des marchés.

items.title: Assurances : les bénéfices bondissent de 21 % en 2025
items.description: Soutenu par la reprise économique et des marchés financiers au sommet, le secteur des assurances affiche une santé financière étincelante au terme de l'exercice 2025. Alors que les profits s'envolent et que la solvabilité franchit des seuils historiques, l'ACAPS s'apprête à faire basculer le marché dans l'ère de la Solvabilité Basée sur les Risques. Bénéficiant d'un contexte macroéconomique favorable marqué par un raffermissement de la croissance nationale à 4,9 %, les compagnies d'assurances et de réassurance ont réalisé un exercice 2025 particulièrement dynamique selon le rapport annuel sur la stabilité financière publié conjointement par Bank Al-Maghrib, l'Autorité de contrôle des assurances et de la prévoyance sociale et l'Autorité marocaine du marché des capitaux . Cette progression s'est traduite par un renforcement simultané des volumes de souscription et de la rentabilité globale des opérateurs. Une envolée des bénéfices tirée par les performances boursières Le chiffre d'affaires global du secteur s'est établi à 63,2 milliards de dirhams, marquant une progression soutenue de 7,5 % par rapport à l'exercice précédent. Cette croissance s'appuie sur la dynamique équilibrée de ses deux grandes branches d'activité. La branche Vie s'inscrit en hausse de 8,4 %, tirée par la solide performance de la collecte Épargne qui grimpe de 8,9 %. De son côté, la branche Non-Vie enregistre une hausse de 6,6 %, portée par la reprise de la consommation et l'extension des couvertures de dommages. Au-delà de l'activité commerciale récurrente, c'est sur le plan financier que le secteur réalise une percée remarquable. Le résultat net de l'industrie s'apprécie de 21,4 % pour atteindre 5,3 milliards de dirhams. Cette hausse spectaculaire découle principalement de l'envolée des marchés actions, l'indice MASI ayant progressé de 27,6 % sur l'année. Ce contexte boursier porteur a permis d'accumuler un gisement de plus-values latentes de 62,5 milliards de dirhams, représentant 23,8 % du portefeuille de placements des assureurs. En conséquence, la rentabilité des fonds propres (ROE) s'élève à 11,1 %, signant son plus haut niveau observé sur la dernière décennie. Solvabilité renforcée et cap sur la régulation SBR à fin 2026 Cette accumulation de plus-values et la très bonne tenue des résultats ont directement consolidé l'assise financière des compagnies. Le ratio réglementaire de solvabilité gagne 54,7 points de pourcentage au cours de l'exercice pour atteindre 409,4 %, assurant une couverture très largement supérieure aux exigences légales minimales. Par ailleurs, les exercices de simulation de crise (stress tests) conduits par l'ACAPS confirment la capacité solide du secteur à absorber des chocs macroéconomiques ou techniques d'ampleur. Fort de ces fondations financières assainies, le secteur aborde une étape charnière de sa modernisation institutionnelle. L'ACAPS a en effet finalisé l'amendement de la circulaire générale relative au nouveau cadre de la Solvabilité Basée sur les Risques (SBR). Sa publication au Bulletin Officiel est programmée pour le début du second semestre 2026, en vue d'une entrée en vigueur effective lors de l'arrêté des comptes au 31 décembre 2026. Ce dispositif réalignera le marché national sur les meilleurs standards prudentiels internationaux en adaptant le capital requis au profil de risque réel de chaque opérateur. The post Assurances : les bénéfices bondissent de 21 % en 2025 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: GMet forecasts thunderstorms in northern Ghana, rain expected in parts of the country
items.description: Thunderstorms accompanied by rain are expected to persist across parts of northern Ghana this evening, with mostly cloudy conditions forecast across the country. According to the weather outlook for Saturday, August 1, 2026, areas within the transition and middle belts are also likely to experience rainfall from this evening into the night. The forecast indicates that patches of mist may develop in some forest and mountainous areas during the early hours of Sunday, potentially reducing visibility. Relatively cool temperatures are also expected across the country during the night and early morning. In southern and coastal Ghana, mostly cloudy conditions are expected in areas including Aflao, Anloga, Accra, Kasoa, Winneba, Cape Coast, Takoradi, Axim, Koforidua, Akim Oda, Kwahu Tafo, Kumasi, Obuasi, Tarkwa and Sefwi Bekwai. Ho is expected to experience drizzle. For the forest and transition zones, thunderstorms with possible rainfall are forecast for Kete Krachi, Atebubu, Ejura, Kintampo, Sunyani and Techiman, while Goaso and Sampa are expected to remain mostly cloudy. In Northern Ghana, thunderstorms with rain are likely in Yendi, Tamale, Bole, Damongo, Bolgatanga, Nalerigu, Wa and Jirapa. The state of the sea is expected to remain calm. The public, particularly motorists, has been advised to exercise caution due to possible reduced visibility in some areas and changing weather conditions.

items.title: Des dizaines d’habitations menacées de démolition par les travaux de réhabilitation des voiries à Matadi
Serigne Abdou Diakhtate, l’érudit au service de Cheikhoul Khadim
items.description: Disciple de Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba, éducateur et poète reconnu, Serigne Mbaye Diakhaté a consacré sa vie à la formation spirituelle des disciples. Retour sur le parcours d’un homme de savoir qui a marqué de son empreinte les premières heures du mouridisme. Trouvé chez lui, au quartier Touba-Ndiarème, Mor Kane Balla Aïssa ne tarit pas d’éloges sur Serigne Mbaye Diakhaté, qu’il présente comme l’un des compagnons les plus érudits de Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba. « C’était un homme de science issu d’une famille où le savoir se transmettait de génération en génération », résume d’emblée le spécialiste du mouridisme. « C’est en 1975 que j’ai découvert Serigne Mbaye à travers deux vers adressés à l’un de ses élèves, Khaly. La profondeur de son message m’avait immédiatement frappé. Je me suis dit alors que l’auteur de ces lignes était appelé à entrer dans la postérité », se souvient-il. Né en 1875 à Keur Makalla, Serigne Babacar Diakhaté, plus connu sous le nom de Serigne Mbaye Diakhaté, est le fils de Khally Madiakhaté Kalla, éminente figure intellectuelle du Cayor et du Baol, et de Sokhna Penda Coumba Fall, fille de Boubacar Penda Yéri Fall, descendant de Khally Amar Fall, fondateur de la prestigieuse université de Pire. « Serigne Mbaye était apparenté à la plupart des grandes familles religieuses et savantes du Sénégal », souligne Mor Kane Balla Aïssa. Très tôt initié aux sciences islamiques par son père puis par son frère aîné Mor Saassoum Diakhaté, le jeune Babacar grandit dans un environnement où l’excellence intellectuelle allait de soi. « Il a vécu 24 ans dans la concession familiale, sous l’aile de son père Khaly Madiakhaté Kalla. La maison de Khaly étant une véritable université, Serigne Mbaye avait sans doute un niveau assez élevé en termes de connaissances avant qu’il n’envisage de rejoindre Serigne Touba », indique le spécialiste. En ce moment, le saint homme était en exil au Gabon, mais Babacar Diakhaté se résolut tout de même de rester avec son frère, Mame Thierno Birahim, qui compléta son enseignement dans plusieurs domaines des sciences. Selon Mor Kane Balla Aïssa, Mame Thierno présenta Serigne Mbaye à Cheikhoul Khadim, à son retour d’exil en 1902, en lui précisant qu’il était le fils de Khally Madiakhaté Kalla, rappelé à Dieu plus tôt en 1900. « Serigne Touba reconnut qu’il devait beaucoup à ce dernier qui fut son professeur. Prendre Serigne Mbaye est donc pour lui une occasion d’exprimer sa reconnaissance à Khaly », précise Mor Kane. Expert de l’âme humaine C’est ainsi que Serigne Mbaye commença son service auprès de Serigne Touba dont il deviendra un disciple de premier plan. En 1903, Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba fut de nouveau déporté en Mauritanie. Le disciple, en compagnie de Serigne Ndame Abdourahmane Lo, n’hésita pas à le rejoindre au pays des maures. Sur place, le Cheikh lui confia la formation et l’éducation de son fils Serigne Bassirou Mbacké. «Je ferai de toi ce que tu veux, à condition de faire de lui, ce que je veux qu’il soit, lui a dit Serigne Touba», précise Mor Kane. C’est dans ce cadre que Serigne Mbaye Diakhaté passa 20 ans auprès de Serigne Touba entre son séjour en Maritanie et bien après son retour durant son installation à Thiéyène Djoloff et, plus tard, à Diourbel. Éducateur hors pair et travailleur infatigable, Serigne Mbaye Diakhaté continua à assister le Cheikh dans la formation des disciples, «au-delà de ses activités agricoles». «C’était un grand érudit spécialisé dans l’éducation de l’âme et la formation spirituelle», précise Mor Kane. Aujourd’hui, son œuvre est reprise par des chanteurs religieux et fait l’objet de recherche dans les milieux académiques. En son temps d’ailleurs, comprenant la dimension éducative des textes de Serigne Mbaye, le Khalife général des mourides, Serigne Abdou Lahad, avait demandé au chanteur Cheikh Ahad Touré d’enregistrer sur cassettes toutes ses œuvres. A cette occasion, selon Mor Kane, plus d’une vingtaine de bandes cassettes ont été ainsi réalisés. « À ce jour, près de 5000 poèmes de Serigne Mbaye sont recensés. Tous abordent des thématiques telles que l’exhortation au travail, la patience, la discipline morale, etc. », précise le spécialiste. Serigne Mbaye Diakahté fut rappelé à Dieu en 1954. Par Souleymane WANE

items.title: Visa pour la France : les Algériens reculent à la 4e position en 2025
items.description: Une nouvelle polémique a éclaté la mi-juillet en France concernant l'octroi des visas aux demandeurs Algériens, donnant l’impression qu'ils figurent parmi les plus importants bénéficiaires, mais la réalité des chiffres est tout autre. L’ambassadeur de France en Algérie, Stéphane Romatet , a évoqué dans un entretien à TSA diffusé mardi 14 juillet la possibilité d’un retour au niveau de délivrances des visas d’avant la crise, c’est-à-dire à peu près 250.000 visas par an. Ces déclarations ont suscité une levée de boucliers de la droite et l’extrême droite françaises. Contrairement au discours de ce courant anti-algérien, les Algériens ne sont pas en tête en termes de visas délivrés par la France. Ils ne figurent même pas dans le top 3 du classement, comme l'indiquent les statistiques de 2025, dévoilées fin juin dernier par le ministre français de l’Intérieur. Les visas pour les Algériens ont connu une courbe contraire à la tendance générale. Visas C pour la France : les Algériens à la 5e place en 2025 L’année 2025 a été marquée par une augmentation de la demande (+ 1,1 %) et de la délivrance de visas (+ 3,5 %). Un total de 2.958.000 visas a été délivré pendant la même année par les représentations consulaires françaises à l'étranger. Le nombre de demandes s'est élevé à 3.524.000. Près de 542.000 demandes ont été refusées. Avec près de 3 millions de visas délivrés, l’année 2025 est à un niveau comparable à 2016, souligne la même source. Cette hausse des délivrances n’a pas profité aux Algériens. En termes de visas de court séjour, le ministère de l’Intérieur indique que 1 visa sur 5 a été délivré à des demandeurs chinois qui ont obtenu au total 541.523 visas. Les Chinois sont suivis des Marocains (267 559 visas). Les Algériens ne sont que cinquièmes du classement avec 185.871 visas, derrière les demandeurs indiens (227 183) et saoudiens (194 091). Derrière les Algériens viennent les Russes (169.000), les Turcs (124.000) et les Tunisiens (100.900). En 2024, la France délivré 250.000 visas aux Algériens les plaçant dans le top 3 derrière les Chinois et les Marocains. Visas long séjour : les Tunisiens devant les Algériens Concernant les visas de long séjour, il se sont élevés en 2025 à 290.772 visas, en hausse légère de 0,9 % par rapport à 2024. Sur ce total, 46,8 % ont été attribués à des ressortissants de pays africains. Cinq pays du continent ont obtenu 30 % des visas de long séjour. Il s’agit du Maroc (32 544), Tunisie (18 942), Algérie (18 371), Cameroun (9 359), et Côte d’Ivoire (7 325). Là encore, la part des Algériens a baissé par rapport à 2024. Les visas de long séjour délivrés à des Algériens sont en grande partie des visas étudiant (48,7 %), tandis que 28,8 % l’ont été pour un motif familial, 9,4 % pour un motif économique et 13,2 % pour des motifs divers. La part des visas pour motif économique monte à 28 % pour les ressortissants marocains et tunisiens. En tout, les Algériens ont bénéficié de 204.242 visas (court séjour et long séjour) en 2025, ce qui correspond à la baisse de 20 % par rapport à 2024 annoncée par Paris il y a quelques jours, et ce qui place l'Algérie à la 4e position derrière la Chine, le Maroc et l'Inde. L’article Visa pour la France : les Algériens reculent à la 4e position en 2025 est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: PPP, PML-N continue war of words on eve of Muzaffarabad elections
items.description: The PPP and the PML-N continued lambasting each other on Saturday, extending their rhetoric from the ongoing elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) to the other party’s previous tenures in power. The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged as the winner in the elections in AJK’s Mirpur division. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling. Political temperatures remain high as the second phase of AJK elections is set to be held tomorrow in nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division. The third phase is scheduled for August 10 in all 12 refugee constituencies and 11 constituencies of Poonch division. In the latest exchange, PML-N senior leader Rana Sanaullah remarked on President Asif Ali Zardari’s role as he responded to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s allegations of rigging in the 2024 general elections . “If you call the votes secured by the prime minister votes of Forms-47, then on what forms has the president gotten votes on?” Sanaullah said. On Wednesday, Bilawal had taken a direct jibe at Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, saying: “If someone is sitting on the PM’s seat, or someone is sitting on the CM’s position today, even a child knows that it is not because of the people’s votes or your performance but because of Form-47.” Sanaullah, also the prime minister’s aide on political affairs and a federal minister, was addressing a gathering in Jhelum Valley alongside Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam. Sanaullah further said: “If you say to Mian Nawaz Sharif that he became the prime minister for the first time or every time through rigging, […] then remember, it is also discussed here that someone also became the prime minister for the first time after breaking apart the country.” He was referring to PPP founder Zulfikar Ali Bhutto , who became the president of Pakistan in December 1971 after the secession of Bangladesh (then-East Pakistan) following the 1970 elections . In August 1973, Bhutto took the oath as the prime minister in 1973 under the new Constitution. Sanaullah also took a jibe at Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, whose recent remarks have sparked a fresh debate in political circles on the matter of creating new provinces. Calling Naqvi a “blessed one” of President Zardari, the PML-N leader said the interior minister had “made the [political] journey of 30 years in three-and-a-half years”. “You began from where and have now reached where, and now you realise that this system is completely dysfunctional.” In his speech, Muqam criticised the PPP’s governance in Sindh, saying that no performance of the party could be seen. He also said the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) — a scheme that the PPP often takes credit for launching — was not “anyone’s personal programme but the government’s”. Earlier on Saturday, PPP leader Saeed Ghani alleged that the PML-N had never won a general election without rigging. This followed a press briefing by Punjab’s education and sports ministers, where they said that the chief ministers of Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had nothing to show for their performance. PML-N never won an election without rigging: Ghani Addressing a press conference in Karachi, Ghani said, “The PPP did not secure power through rigging in any of the elections held till today. “On the other hand, however many times the PML-N has secured power, it has not been without rigging.” PPP leader Saeed Ghani addresses a press conference in Karachi on Aug 1, 2026. — DawnNewsTV Ghani, also the Sindh labour minister, made the allegation as he responded to a PML-N member calling on the PPP to not “give lectures on democracy”. “If you do not want to give the PPP the right to speak on democracy, then will you give it to Gen Musharraf or Gen Zia, or the leaders created by them?” he quipped, referring to the two former military dictators. The PPP leader said he “did count the 1985 election”, alleging that PML-N supremo and ex-premier Nawaz Sharif “conspired” against ex-prime minister Mohammad Khan Junejo . He further claimed that his party “became a target of rigging” in the 1988 and 1990 elections , which resulted in the PML-N winning. He went on to allege that the PPP was again “controlled and prevented from forming a government in Punjab” in 1993. Ghani alleged that the PPP was restricted to “16-17 seats” in the 1997 general elections , when Nawaz’s PML-N again formed the government. He contended that although the PPP secured power in 2008, the “PML-N was made to win seats, especially in Punjab, through rigging during Musharraf’s tenure”. Ghani claimed that the PML-N was “made to win” the 2013 elections as well. “Then the elections in 2024 [took place]. No matter how many times they say, everyone, even children, know that the PML-N was badly defeated in the elections,” he asserted. The PPP leader alleged that Nawaz, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz “lost their own seats and then blame us”. Ghani made the remarks after explaining the rationale for his party’s stances on new provinces in Sindh and Punjab, stressing that it was based on the wishes of the people. He emphasised that the Constitution required any such move to be made through the elected representatives in the provincial assembly concerned. He noted that the “people of Sindh, its representatives and its assembly say there is no need for further provinces in Sindh”. On the other hand, Ghani pointed out, the Punjab Assembly and the Senate had passed resolutions over a decade ago calling for two new provinces in Punjab. “If the people and the elected representatives of Sindh say that there is no need for any new province in Sindh, then no one in Punjab has the right to say whether there should be a new province in Sindh or not,” Ghani asserted. He went on to stress that the PPP advocated for more provinces in Punjab as the “people of Punjab and their elected representatives” desired that. The PPP leader emphasised that his party “represented” the citizens of each of the provinces when taking a stance for Sindh and Punjab. At the outset of his press conference, Ghani also took exception to comments made by “two ministers”, saying it seemed that they “did not know anything about Sindh”. “They are restricted within a circle called Maryam Nawaz. They only see and say what she tells them, shows them and explains to them,” he said in an apparent reference to the Punjab ministers.

items.title: ‘Enough is enough’: MQM-P leaders, Shahid Khaqan back creation of new administrative units
items.description: Former premier Shahid Khaqan Abbasi and MQM-P leaders Dr Farooq Sattar and Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui on Saturday backed the creation of additional administrative units in the country. On Thursday, Naqvi urged all political parties to “settle” various national-level issues, including the question of creating new provinces . Addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 being held in Islamabad, Naqvi said there was “only one solution” to improving the country’s overall condition: “You will have to take [the matter of] administrative units, provinces or whatever you may call it, to the public.” Addressing a press conference in Karachi today, MQM leader Dr Farooq Sattar said that, due to immense population growth, additional administrative units were essential to ensure proper governance. “No country in the world has seen population growth as fast as ours,” he said. “We need to manage and administer that, but how will we do that without additional administrative units?” Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui and MQM Deputy Convener Dr Farooq Sattar address a press conference in Karachi on August 1, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/Dawn News Sattar noted that, with such a large population, questions arose about how administrations would be able to address fundamental issues and ensure effective service delivery. “Two things have become clear: we need administrative units. Enough is enough,” he declared. “The ad-hocism we have seen for around 80 years must end. [Interior Minister] Mohsin Naqvi presented a clear administrative framework for Pakistan’s future in his speech, which is welcomed by citizens from all walks of life.” “Pakistan’s economy is tied to its political and administrative structure.” “We need curative treatment, not symptomatic treatment,” he stated. Sattar added that the door needs to be left open for Gen-Z to play a representative role in Pakistan’s political, economic and social landscape. “Political parties should move in this direction, as they are of the opinion that the system is infertile; it cannot ensure people’s prosperity or progress, build national consensus or strength, or guarantee the country’s security,” he stated. “If we want to avail ourselves of these benefits, Pakistan must walk among the world with its head held high; the youth have to stand on their feet; we have to look the world and the IMF (International Monetary Fund) in the eye and talk to them. New administrative units are essential for this; without them, we will not move forward.” Speaking before Sattar, Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui noted that the conference addressed by Naqvi was an economic one, not a political one. “We understand that there are no higher administrative units other than districts and divisions within a province. With One Unit, provinces were dissolved, but they returned after the end of the One Unit scheme in a different form,” he said, addressing the press conference. “This issue of the limits of administrative units never existed, nor was it part of Pakistan’s politics. Are these [units] so sacred that we cannot talk about them? When nobody spoke about them, we did,” Siddiqui added. He also stated that no matter which province people live in, they are still living within Pakistan, noting that the state itself is indivisible. “The Constitution demands the division of provinces. But because of the pressure from a growing population, the procedures outlined in 1973 can no longer be enforced. This is why the MQM submitted an amendment bill in the National Assembly; it was not opposed and has been supported by the standing committee,” Siddiqui said. “This MQM demand, which is in accordance with Pakistan’s population growth, is an administrative necessity and addresses the country’s economic issues,” he added. “Our voice is being echoed by others. Today, we thank you all for highlighting this need during the month of Pakistan’s independence.” Siddiqui said the party further believed that the current system of democracy, “where benefits never reach the people”, was not needed. Ex-PM Abbasi says system needs to be changed Former prime minister and Awaam Pakistan convener Shahid Khaqan Abbasi also addressed a press conference at the National Press Club in Islamabad, stating that the current state of affairs could not continue for much longer, but noted that the government was beginning to realise it. “I am grateful to my interior minister for acknowledging after four or five years that the country is not running,” he stated. “It should have been discussed in parliament or the cabinet. The country knows it is not running, but it has finally dawned on the rulers.” Abbasi added that the military’s spokesperson had acknowledged this during his press conference on Friday and that reform was the only way to keep the country functioning, but “there are always people who do not want meaningful change”. “This is a matter of interests; if we talk about reforms in this country, then those whose interests do not align with reforms will oppose them,” he added. “The country is not being run well; we do not have money, and we are not ready to undertake reforms. “Reforms are needed in this country; otherwise, the situation will get worse. Your debts, costs and taxes will continue to increase.” Abbasi noted that simply creating new provinces would not solve the issue, but that the entire system needed to be changed. “After 78 years, we don’t know how to buy flour. Our farmers have been ruined, and today we are even importing wheat by spending precious dollars,” he said, alleging that those in power were more interested in purchasing official vehicles and aircraft than addressing the hardships faced by ordinary citizens. He stressed that constitutional supremacy and the rule of law were necessary for political stability and economic growth. “Without the rule of law, investment will not come, and without investment there can be no sustainable economic progress,” Abbasi said. ‘Better late than never’ In a post on X, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif voiced his agreement with Naqvi on the matter of new provinces, but criticised the interior minister for failing to raise the issue earlier and for not implementing the 12 points of the National Action Plan that fall within his remit. “As a political worker, I also strongly feel that the system’s evolutionary process has, for decades, remained subject to group and personal interests. It needs to be freed from those influences,” he wrote. Asif also suggested that the matter be discussed in both parliament and the cabinet, adding that doing so would strengthen institutions and the system, while any changes would proceed through the constitutional process. “Mr Naqvi is a highly respected and influential member of the cabinet. That said, it is generally acknowledged that he attends meetings of both parliament and the cabinet only occasionally,” he noted. “In my opinion, sidelining these institutions and instead inviting the country’s distinguished and respected business leaders to speak before a captive audience on such an important issue does not carry the same weight or receive the same recognition as discussing it in the relevant constitutional forums,” Asif stated. Asif added that Naqvi had held powerful positions in Pakistani politics for the past three-and-a-half years and could have initiated a discussion or made progress towards systemic reform during that time. “Nevertheless, better late than never.” Asif also referred to a press conference by ISPR chief Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, who mentioned the 13 points of the National Action Plan. “One of those points — which was the responsibility of our armed forces — is being implemented and fulfilled through the sacrifice of lives. The remaining 12 points fall under the responsibility of the Ministry of Interior, and they have not been implemented,” he noted. “Mr Naqvi should begin reforming the system by implementing the National Action Plan. Let systemic change begin with his own ministry. It is not only our respected business community — the entire nation stands with him.” Various political parties have demanded the creation of more provinces or administrative units to ensure better governance. The MQM-P — an ally of the PML-N-led ruling coalition — has been demanding that Karachi be designated a province separate from Sindh. However, the PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre along with MQM-P, has strongly opposed the suggested move. On the other hand, the PPP and the PTI have long advocated for a South Punjab province . A day prior, Inter-Services Public Relations chief Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry commented on Naqvi’s remarks about the need for new administrative units in Pakistan: “We have been saying this earlier also as a primary stakeholder in security that good governance is essential for the security and stability of Pakistan.” “Now our population is 240-250 million people, and we still have four provinces. We have to see whether this is serving the purpose of good governance. That debate has to be sensibly held by politicians, by those in power, even those who have previously been in power, and those who are responsible to the people of Pakistan,” the DG ISPR said, adding that it had to be done according to the will of the people of Pakistan. Later on Friday, PPP Secretary-General Nayyar Bokhari said that the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) will deliberate on creating new administrative units, which should be created through the mechanism provided in the Constitution rather than by executive order. “The Constitution of Pakistan has clearly laid down the complete procedure. Without a two-thirds majority in the relevant provincial assembly, the National Assembly and the Senate, neither the creation of new provinces nor any alteration in provincial boundaries is possible,” he told Dawn . “New provinces cannot be created through an executive order. They can only be created through a constitutional decision of parliament,” he added. Additional reporting by Ikram Junaidi

items.title: Spain attacks ‘selfish’ response of some EU countries to Ceuta migrant crossings
items.description: Spain has condemned the “selfish, polarising and unlawful” reaction of some EU countries to the influx of about 60,000 migrants from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. Spanish officials say almost all those who reached Ceuta on 30 July have returned, while Spain’s interior minister said on Saturday that the death toll from the surge in crossings had risen to at least 67. Italy temporarily suspended the EU’s border-free Schengen arrangement with Spain, as PM Giorgia Meloni called the scenes “shocking”. Finland and Denmark backed Italy’s move, while Czech PM Andrej Babiš urged a temporary suspension of Spain’s Schengen membership. EU interior ministers will meet on Tuesday by video conference to discuss the issue. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez had called for an urgent meeting to “reaffirm that the security of our external borders is a shared responsibility of all Member States”. Twenty-two of the EU’s 27 countries also called for emergency talks in an open letter, citing “serious concerns” regarding the developments in Ceuta. The nations “welcome that Spain and Morocco are cooperating closely to ensure the swift return of migrants”, but said a video conference would help reach agreement on mobilising EU instruments and support for Spain to restore “effective control” of the border and prevent further uncontrolled crossings. In a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said he had “serious concerns” about some European governments. He said the Spanish government had fully restored control over the border and prevented any “unauthorised onward movement towards continental Europe” in less than 48 hours. While most had shown “support and solidarity”, Sanchez said other European governments had chosen to attack Spain, “driven by prejudice, fake news, ignorance, or political interest”, and pointed out that Ceuta was not part of the Schengen area. “The European Union cannot afford this kind of selfish, polarising and unlawful reaction,” he said. Also on Saturday, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he had spoken to Sánchez and the UK was “providing what help we can”. Spain says it has fully regained control of its border following the mass crossings into Ceuta There were chaotic scenes on Thursday in Ceuta as border controls in the North African enclave apparently broke down. But in a news conference on Saturday, Spain’s Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska told reporters the situation in Ceuta had almost returned to normal. “Almost all of [the migrants] have already left Ceuta,” the minister said, adding that businesses had now reopened. “The situation has been almost entirely reversed.” He also said Spain had started to establish an inflatable maritime barrier to prevent further illegal migrant entry. Spanish police officers and soldiers escort a large group of migrants in Ceuta to the border to take them out of Spain. But while the situation on the ground appears to be easing, political and diplomatic fallout is rippling through Madrid and other capitals. On Thursday, Italy’s Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on social media that such “uncontrolled immigration” was a threat to national security, before suspending the Schengen zone agreement with Spain for a month. The Schengen Area is a system of open borders spanning 29 European countries that have abolished controls at their common borders. Spain responded by summoning the Italian ambassador to Madrid, while its foreign minister said he expected “European solidarity and not partisan demagoguery”. Finland’s Interior Minister Mari Rantanen said she had started preparations for restoring internal border checks “if the need arises”. She also urged “all European countries” to support Meloni’s move. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen also urged the EU to “consider all options, including a suspension of Schengen co-operation”. France has tightened checks on its border with Spain and said it would increase its police presence by Saturday. Portuguese PM Luis Montenegro said he was considering reinforcing border checks. Von der Leyen said the images from Ceuta were “unacceptable”. “We cannot allow anyone to come to our Union without abiding by our rules,” she said on social media. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he “supports Spain’s intention not to allow illegal migrants onto the European continent”, and demanded that Morocco “take back illegal migrants immediately”. In the US, the State Department said the incident was a direct result of Spain’s migration policies. President Donald Trump called the situation a “catastrophe” and said, “it looks like an invasion of a country by hundreds of thousands of people”. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez blamed trafficking gangs for the migrant surge in Ceuta. Spain has defended its handling of the migrant surge. Madrid has sent troops, more police, drones, divers and boats to Ceuta. The country has also deployed its armed forces to bolster security in another Spanish enclave, Melilla, where hundreds of crossings were also reported. Sánchez, who has visited Ceuta after the migrant influx, said he would consider reinforcing the border with Morocco, and that Moroccan authorities were co-operating. He blamed trafficking gangs for the migrant surge, calling the incident a “violation of Spain’s territorial integrity”. “Trafficking mafias took a self-serving interpretation of a Supreme Court ruling” which “spread like wildfire”, he said. EU Commissioner Magnus Brunner said, after a phone call with Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares, that “not a single person has crossed to mainland EU”. In June, Spain’s Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla could not be summarily returned to Morocco without due process. While the surge of migrants this year is extraordinary, Ceuta has long been a focal point for migrants attempting to reach Europe. During the summer months, there is often a big push to reach Ceuta, typically organised over social media. In 2021, about 8,000 people entered Ceuta over a matter of days, exacerbating Spain’s diplomatic tensions with Morocco. Morocco, which has been suffering from a high unemployment rate, witnessed several Gen Z anti-government protests last year, with young people demanding better opportunities and improvements to public services. Together with Melilla, Ceuta forms the European Union’s only land borders with Africa. Migrants can enter the enclave by swimming several kilometres. Spain has a relatively friendly approach to immigration. In April, the government approved plans to give legal status to 500,000 undocumented migrants, allowing them to be formally integrated into the workforce. At that time, the right-wing Italian prime minister had already criticised Sánchez, saying the policy would “affect its neighbours”. In June the European Parliament approved tougher migration rules that grant authorities broader powers to return irregular arrivals.

items.title: Rentrée scolaire 2026 : les enseignants contractuels menacent de bloquer l’ouverture des classes
items.description: « Tant qu'il n'y a pas d'arrêté d'engagement, il n'y aura pas de cours. Terminé ! » menacent les enseignements contractuels. À quelques semaines de la rentrée scolaire prévue en septembre, le collectif des enseignants contractuels communaux non retenus, hausse le ton. Réunis ce samedi 1er août 2026 à la Bourse du Travail de Kaloum, ses membres ont lancé un avertissement au gouvernement, exigeant la signature de leur arrêté d'engagement avant la reprise des cours. À défaut, ils annoncent des actions pouvant compromettre l'ouverture effective des classes sur l'ensemble du territoire. Cette mobilisation intervient alors que les commissions chargées d'examiner leur dossier, mises en place en avril dernier par le gouvernement, en collaboration avec l'intersyndicale de l'éducation, n'ont toujours pas achevé le processus d'intégration des enseignants concernés. Au cours de la rencontre, les manifestants ont réaffirmé deux principales revendications : la correction immédiate des anomalies relevées sur les listes et la finalisation du processus d'intégration « sans exclusion, sans omission, sans substitution et sans retard » , sous le slogan : « Notre Arrêté d'Engagement maintenant ! » . Un ultimatum adressé au gouvernement Prenant la parole au nom du collectif, le coordinateur Diaka Sow a fixé une ligne rouge. Il a demandé que les arrêtés d'engagement soient signés durant les vacances scolaires, faute de quoi, une nouvelle phase de mobilisation sera engagée. « Si notre arrêté d'engagement n'est pas signé pendant ces vacances, nous allons faire recours à l'intersyndicale de l’éducation » , a-t-il averti. S'adressant ensuite aux responsables syndicaux présents, il a insisté sur l'urgence du dossier : « Nous vous invitons rapidement à défendre notre dossier auprès du gouvernement. Faites tout votre possible pour que l'arrêté de 4 500 enseignants soit signé pendant ces vacances. A défaut de cela, vous allez nous permettre de déclencher une grève générale et illimitée. » Le coordinateur est allé encore plus loin en menaçant directement la rentrée scolaire. « Tant qu'il n'y a pas d'arrêté d'engagement, il n'y aura pas de cours. Terminé ! » , a-t-il lancé devant les enseignants mobilisés. Dans le même élan, Diaka Sow a interpellé le président de la République afin qu'une solution soit rapidement trouvée à leur situation. « J’adresse une plaidoirie au président Mamadi Doumbouya, père de tous les 4 000 enseignants contractuels. On est soumis à l'éthique du pays, on est parti enseigner dans les villages. Aujourd'hui, on a fait le concours spécifique à la pratique de classe et on a obtenu la moyenne requise » , a-t-il déclaré. Le SLECG évoque un problème de moyens Présent à cette rencontre, Mohamed Bangoura, responsable de la communication du Syndicat Libre des Enseignants et Chercheurs de Guinée (SLECG), a apporté des précisions sur les raisons du retard enregistré dans le traitement des dossiers. Selon lui, les commissions ont déjà largement avancé dans leur travail, mais se heurtent désormais à un manque de moyens logistiques et financiers, indispensables pour achever les dernières vérifications sur le terrain. « Le gouvernement nous a donné deux mois renouvelables une fois, pour le traitement de votre dossier. Nous nous sommes dit, c'est le terrain qui commande. Deux mois renouvelables une fois, c'est-à-dire quatre mois. Et allez-y, comparez, les jours sont payés à 350 000. Nous nous sommes dit, entre nous, ce n'est pas la somme de 350 000 par 30 mois qui va faire de nous des hommes nantis. Derrière, il y a nos sœurs, nos frères, nos tantes, nos neveux, qui n'attendent que le compte rendu de cette commission pour avoir un espoir. Nous nous sommes dit, quatre mois, c'est trop. Il faut réduire le travail à deux semaines. Si nous allons avoir de l'argent, ce n'est pas sur le dos de ces pauvres enseignants qui souffrent et qui pleurent. Nous nous sommes dit, il n'est plus question d'aller au MEPUA ou d'appeler pour la remontée des listes. » Poursuivant son intervention, le responsable syndical a assuré que le travail technique est pratiquement achevé, tout en expliquant que la dernière étape dépend désormais de l'appui du gouvernement. « Et au moment où je vous parle, de Conakry à Genève et de Genève à Conakry, nous avons fini de traiter votre dossier. Et nous nous sommes dit, après la publication de cette liste, il ne faudrait pas entendre quelqu'un dire, vous m'avez oublié. Alors, voici ce qui explique le retard. Nous avons demandé simplement à la Commission de négociation de mettre les moyens logistiques et financiers à notre disposition afin que nous puissions aller dans la dernière sous-préfecture de la Guinée pour savoir si on n'a pas oublié quelqu'un derrière nous » , a rassuré Mohamed Bangoura.

items.title: Second phase of AJK elections on Sunday in 9 Muzaffarabad division, 12 refugee constituencies
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: Polling for the second phase of elections to the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly will be held on Sunday in nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 constituencies reserved for Kashmiri refugees settled in Pakistan, where more than 340 candidates are contesting 21 seats. According to the AJK Election Commission, 207 candidates are in the fray for the nine constituencies in Muzaffarabad division, comprising five seats in Muzaffarabad district and two each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts. Another 137 candidates are contesting the 12 refugee constituencies, including six seats representing refugees from the Kashmir Valley and six from Jammu. A total of 809,621 voters are registered in Muzaffarabad division, including 427,955 men and 381,666 women. The 12 refugee constituencies have a combined electorate of 438,834, comprising 247,776 male and 191,054 female voters. Internet services were suspended again on Friday, less than 45 hours after being restored, as part of efforts to discourage elements attempting to disrupt the election process. Official sources said the services were likely to be restored on Sunday. However, the Election Commission made it clear that polling would be held as scheduled in all nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and the 12 refugee constituencies. It added that polling would continue from 8am to 5pm without a break. Election material had been delivered to all polling stations in the 12 refugee constituencies, the commission said, adding that the distribution of polling material had also been completed in all constituencies of Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts, while the process had entered its final stage in the five constituencies of Muzaffarabad district. Polling staff had also been dispatched to their respective polling stations under stringent security arrangements. According to the commission, 1,483 polling stations have been established across Muzaffarabad division, of which 533 have been declared highly sensitive, 741 sensitive and 209 normal. Another 1,057 polling stations have been set up for the 12 refugee constituencies. It said all administrative and security arrangements had been completed and security personnel had already been deployed at polling stations to ensure the peaceful conduct of polling. Separately, in a televised message to the public on the eve of polling, Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal urged voters to exercise their right to franchise, saying the vote was the only means through which citizens could choose a better future and capable leadership. “There is no substitute for the vote, and every citizen should fulfil this national responsibility,” he said, adding that the vote was a trust that should be entrusted to an honest and competent candidate. Mughal appealed to the electorate to participate wholeheartedly in the democratic process and demonstrate responsible citizenship. He said all arrangements had been finalised to ensure peaceful, transparent and fair elections. During the first phase of elections in Mirpur division, the PML-N grabbed nine out of the 13 constituencies. Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on June 27. Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polling process, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice. According to preliminary results issued by the AJK Election Commission (Forms-27), the PML-N emerged as the winner in nine constituencies, while the PPP could secure only four seats.

items.title: AMVPPC | L’opération de nettoyage des sites archéologiques se poursuit à Carthage
items.description: L'Agence de mise en valeur du patrimoine et de promotion culturelle (AMVPPC) poursuit sa vaste campagne d'entretien et de désherbage à travers les différents sites archéologiques de la cité antique de Carthage. Actuellement concentrées aux abords des célèbres Ports Puniques, ces interventions sont confiées à une entreprise spécialisée mandatée par les services de l'Agence. Le programme d'action comprend notamment le nettoyage approfondi des espaces, l'élimination systématique des herbes parasites ainsi que l'élagage des arbres d'ornement. Cette initiative s'inscrit dans le cadre d'un plan global visant à préserver la qualité paysagère et environnementale des sites archéologiques, en vue d'offrir aux visiteurs et touristes des conditions d'accueil optimales, tout en contribuant activement à la sauvegarde et à la valorisation du patrimoine historique exceptionnel de Carthage. items.title: Nigeria needs leaders who respect public office – Tunde Bakare
items.description: Pastor Tunde Bakare, Founder and Chairman of the Citadel School of Government (CSG), on Saturday said that his greatest desire is to witness a Nigeria that works for every Nigerian. Bakare said this at the graduation ceremony of the CSG pioneer students at the institution’s premises in Oregun, Lagos. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the students graduated with Advanced Diploma in Public Leadership and Statecraft for a nine-month course that began on Sept. 6, 2025. Bakare, the Serving Overseer of the Citadel Global Community Church (CGCC) said that he remained confident that a Nigeria that works would emerge in his lifetime. He said: “We are approaching another significant electoral cycle in Nigeria. Across this country, new leaders will emerge at different levels of government. “Existing leaders will confront increasingly complex demands. “The challenges are immense—insecurity, economic instability, decaying infrastructure, institutional weakness, and a crisis of trust between the governed and those who govern. “I am convinced that the solution to these challenges is not more of the same. The solution is leaders who understand that public office is a sacred trust, not personal enterprise. “Leaders, who prioritise common good over private gain; and have the competence to translate vision into policy, and courage to translate policy into results.” To the graduating students, Bakare said they represented the new breed of leaders, who would break the cycle of incompetence and corruption. The serving overseer said they were leaving with something far more valuable than a document. The cleric said they were leaving with a framework for thinking about governance that transcended political parties, ethnic loyalties and sectional interests, adding that they had been equipped to see the big picture. According to him, the quality of a nation is inseparable from the quality of the people, who exercise leadership within its institutions. “You are leaving with a charge to serve—not to dominate, not to accumulate, not to exploit. You have been trained to lead with integrity, to govern with competence, and to serve with humility. “These are not empty words. They are the foundation upon which this institution was built. “Nigeria is waiting for you. You are the ones who will bring fresh ideas, ethical standards and a commitment to excellence into the corridors of power. “You are the ones who will demonstrate that governance can be different—that it can be responsive, responsible and transformative,” he said. Bakare pointed out that all leaders need to understand that leadership was a calling and not a career. He explained that true leadership was about answering the call to serve something larger than yourself—their community, nation and generation. Bakare urged them not to forget that the people they lead were not stepping stones to their success, adding that they were the very reason for their service, hence the need for integrity. Also speaking, the Executive Director of CSG, Mr Omoaholo Omoakhalen, said that the institution produced 69 pioneer graduands. Omoakhalen urged them to justify the confidence reposed in them by helping to build a Nigeria that works. In a goodwill message, the Executive Director of the Lagos Business School, Prof. Sunday Adebisi, said that the future of Nigeria depends on the quality of leaders entrusted to handle the affairs of the nation. Adebisi said there is a need to bridge the governance challenges in Nigeria and the capacity of its leadership. He said that to advance national development, there is need for leaders who know how to mobilise resources and make it work. In his keynote address, the Vice Chancellor of Caleb University, Prof. Olalekan Asikhia, reiterated the call for a new breed of leaders. The Vice Chancellor said that there is need to redefine leadership in Nigeria as a responsibility and not a title. The professor, who spoke on ‘Institutional Excellence and Fragile Institutions’, called for true leadership with an ability to steer the people in the right direction and build strong institutions. “The gap between theory and practical must be filled. We need builders who would focus on building systems that will outlive them,” he said. NAN reports that goodwill messages were also delivered by other guests, including Dr Joe Okei-Odumakin. (NAN) The post Nigeria needs leaders who respect public office – Tunde Bakare appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja killed in Pakistan avalanche, his company says
items.description: Renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja is among 10 people killed in an avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan, his company has said. Elite Expeditions said it confirmed with “profound sadness and immense heartbreak” that Purja, 43, had died in Thursday’s avalanche. His brother Kamal later wrote: “We will miss you every single day”. Purja, who was born in Nepal and later served in the British army, was known for scaling the world’s 14 highest peaks in just over six months in 2019. Pakistani officials earlier said the bodies of three climbers from his expedition – American Mallory Geis, Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy from Oman and Pur Bahadur Gurung from Nepal – had been recovered. Purja’s death was also confirmed by Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who said that “the tragic death of six Nepalese and four other foreign climbers, including world record holder Nirmal Purja, in the Karakoram mountain range of Pakistan, has shocked us”. “The history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring,” the prime minister added. In a statement, Purja’s older brother Kamal wrote: “It is with the heaviest heart that I share the devastating news that my beloved younger brother, Nirmal ‘Nimsdai’ Purja, and the other climbers are no longer with us. “Although our hearts are broken, we are incredibly proud of you. Your legacy will live forever,” he added. UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: “Incredibly sad to learn of the passing of Nirmal (Nims) Purja and those he was climbing with. “He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years – and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over.” Naila Kiani, a spokesperson for the Alpine Club of Pakistan which is involved in the rescue efforts, told BBC’s Newshour programme that Purja had led many expeditions that she was on. Praising his leadership skills, she described him as a “very experienced climber and fearless”. Kiani said the Alpine Club would only announce his death once the body has been recovered – but she added that “we are fearing them all dead”. She also said rescuers had seen some bodies – but were yet to reach them. Teams in Pakistan have been searching for the climbers on the world’s 12th-highest summit after an avalanche on the 8,047m (26,400ft) peak in the Karakoram range. The multinational climbing group was being led by Purja. Also known as Nims, he rose to prominence in 2019 when he climbed all 14 of the world’s mountains with peaks above 8,000m in 189 days – smashing the previous record by more than seven years. He became widely known following a Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, released two years later. At the time, he said: “It has been a gruelling but humbling six months, and I hope to have proven that anything is possible with some determination, self-belief and positivity.” Purja served in the British military for 16 years, 10 of which were spent in the special forces, and he was awarded an MBE by the late Queen in 2018 for his achievement in extreme high-altitude mountaineering. Purja, who lived with his wife and three-year-old daughter in Hampshire in southern England, said he was also the first Gurkha to climb Everest while serving in the British military. In his last post on X, published on Monday, he said he had not intended to climb Broad Peak. “Initially, the plan was to climb just G2,” Purja wrote, referring to Gasherbrum II, another peak in the Karakoram mountain range. But right before he set off for Pakistan, he realised that if he also managed to climb Broad Peak while he was there, he would have only one more mountain to conquer before becoming the “first person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice. Without oxygen.” An eight-thousander is a mountain that rises more than 8,000m above sea level. “This wasn’t planned,” Purja wrote. “But opportunities don’t scream: they whisper to those already working in silence.” “Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down. I take zero mountains for granted,” he wrote. Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for climbers. The first successful ascent was in 1957, when an Austrian expedition reached the summit. Since then, many more have climbed the mountain, but dozens have lost their lives. One of Broad Peak’s deadliest years was 2013, when at least six fatalities were recorded.

items.title: From punishment to purpose: Meet the Ghanaian artisan turning school cane into décor
items.description: Cane. For many Ghanaians who grew up in the 1990s and 2000s, the word brings back memories of the classroom and the headmaster’s office. But for Doreen Demuyakor, that same cane has become a tool of healing, expression and artistic creativity. Since 2023, the Accra-based artisan has been transforming cane into abstract wall hangings, decorative mirrors and bespoke interior décor pieces that are attracting the attention of design enthusiasts across the city. “I use cane because it is the medium I’m able to express myself the most with,” Demuyakor said. “Besides, I thought it would be the best use for something that traumatised students and children in schools and homes,” she added. According to Demuyakor, her craft journey was not planned. She describes herself as naturally dexterous and someone who has always found joy in creating things with her hands. She spent hours watching woodworkers on social media, fascinated by how they transformed raw materials into beautiful creations. The turning point came during a casual conversation with her former boss. “On a random day, he asked me what I really wanted to do with my life. I didn’t think twice before answering that I wanted to be a carpenter,” she recalled with a laugh. Surprised by her response, her former boss gave her a challenge: to make a mirror. She chose cane for the frame, used a picture she found online as inspiration, and recreated it. He loved the outcome and later requested a bigger piece. “After that, he gave me six months to go and understudy a cane craft master. That was the beginning of who you see today,” she said. Three years on, Demuyakor has developed a unique style. She does not always sketch her designs first or plan every curve before starting a piece. “I’m inspired by everyday objects I interact with. But my most iconic creations have been the ones I set out with no idea of what I’m about to create. I let the canes lead me, and I make changes and corrections as I go,” she explained. That improvisation is what makes her work stand out, creating flowing, organic pieces that transform a rigid material into something soft and expressive. From a symbol of discipline to a centrepiece in modern living spaces, Demuyakor is proving that with creativity, even painful memories can be rewoven into something beautiful.

items.title: NACOC arrests 10 over alleged cannabis distribution at KTU SRC Week celebration
items.description: The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has arrested 10 people for allegedly distributing cannabis and cannabis-infused products during the Students’ Representative Council (SRC) Week celebrations at the Koforidua Technical University (KTU). The suspects, comprising nine men and one woman, were arrested on Friday night during an intelligence-led operation following reports of suspected drug-related activities on the university campus. According to NACOC, the operation led to the seizure of a quantity of suspected cannabis and several consumable products believed to have been infused with the narcotic. The items recovered included wraps of suspected cannabis, cups of “abele” ice cream, bottles of pineapple juice, sobolo drinks, fresh palm wine and other beverages. The Commission said preliminary field tests conducted on the seized exhibits indicated the presence of cannabis, reinforcing suspicions that the products were being distributed to revellers during the celebrations. The 10 suspects are currently assisting with investigations as NACOC works to determine the full extent of the alleged operation and identify any other individuals who may be connected to the suspected illegal drug distribution network. The Commission reaffirmed its commitment to protecting educational institutions from drug-related activities and urged students and members of the public to remain vigilant by reporting suspicious activities to the appropriate authorities.

items.title: Concert de la résilience et du triomphe à Manga : le MCCAT réaffirme le rôle de la culture dans la consolidation de la paix
items.description: Concert de la résilience et du triomphe à Manga : le MCCAT réaffirme le rôle de la culture dans la consolidation de la paix ‎ ‎Le Ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme (MCCAT), Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO a pris part, dans la soirée du vendredi 31 juillet 2026, au Concert de la résilience et du triomphe organisé par l'Orchestre de la Présidence du Faso à la place de la nation de Manga, chef-lieu de la région du Nazinon. ‎ ‎Dans son allocution d'ouverture, le Chef d'orchestre de la Présidence du Faso, le Commandant Aimé Césaire Boezemwendé OUÉDRAOGO a indiqué que cette soirée allait au-delà d'une simple célébration musicale. Selon lui, ce concert rend hommage à la résilience du peuple burkinabè et rappelle, à travers la musique, les valeurs d'espérance, d'unité et de fraternité qui fondent la Nation. ‎ ‎Portée par une forte mobilisation des populations de la cité de l'épervier et des localités environnantes, la soirée s'est déroulée dans une ambiance de ferveur patriotique. Au rythme des chansons de résilience et d'unité interprétées par l'Orchestre de la Présidence du Faso, le public a repris en chœur plusieurs morceaux. Plusieurs figures de la musique burkinabè ont également pris part au spectacle, renforçant le caractère fédérateur de cette célébration culturelle. ‎ ‎Prenant la parole, le Ministre Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO a rappelé que l'Orchestre de la Présidence du Faso s'inscrit dans la vision du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, de promouvoir un réarmement culturel fondé sur la valorisation des arts et des valeurs nationales. Qualifiant cet ensemble musical de véritable ambassadeur de la culture burkinabè, il a salué la qualité de ses prestations, la mise en valeur du Faso Dan Fani et l'expression de la diversité culturelle nationale, autant d'atouts qui contribuent à son rayonnement au Burkina Faso et à l'international. ‎ ‎Le Ministre a, par ailleurs, invité les populations du Nazinon à être des acteurs engagés de la transformation du Burkina Faso, à travers le patriotisme, le civisme et le changement de comportement. Il a enfin réaffirmé le rôle stratégique de la communication et de la culture dans la consolidation de la paix et de la souveraineté nationale. « Nous allons gagner la guerre par les armes, nous allons gagner la paix par la communication et nous allons consolider cette paix par la culture », a-t-il déclaré, avant d'inviter les populations à demeurer unies autour des idéaux de souveraineté, de dignité et de développement. ‎ ‎DCRP/MCCAT #Com_Gouv_BF

items.title: Business… Mondial ! (Le billet de Salla GUÈYE)
items.description: Le football avait déjà vendu son âme aux droits Tv. Voilà qu’il cherche maintenant un acquéreur pour son cœur. À la Fifa, le Mondial n’est plus un trophée, c’est une start-up en quête de levée de fonds. Gianni Infantino promet de « développer le football ». Traduction : transformer le ballon rond en action cotée. Demain, après le Ballon d’Or, place au Ballon en Bourse ! L’Uefa crie au sacrilège, menace de boycott et découvre soudain les vertus de la morale… après des années à compter ses milliards. La CAF, elle, demande d’abord à voir le prospectus. En Afrique, on connaît la chanson. Quand un riche parle d’« opportunité historique », mieux vaut vérifier où est écrit le petit astérisque. Le plus savoureux reste cette idée d’offrir des parts aux fédérations ; chacune pourra garder son morceau… ou le revendre. Le football devient une copropriété où l’on négocie les cages avant même le coup d’envoi. La prochaine Coupe du monde risque de ne plus se jouer sur la pelouse, mais au conseil d’administration. Et le vrai vainqueur soulèvera moins la Coupe… que le cours de l’action. salla.gueye@lesoleil.sn
